note: Frozen BEFORE candidate testing. The launch decision recomputes eligibility from this file plus validated measurements; nothing in an evidence manifest may select its own requirements. Changing any value here is a product decision that invalidates every receipt collected under the previous hash.

scope.decision: Version 3 WIDENS the promise back to its full advertised boundary and makes it non-narrowable: seven vendor clients on three native operating systems, twenty-one cells, no waivers. Version 2 had narrowed the promise to Claude Code on macOS and named the rest preview; that narrowing is removed, and with it the `uncertified` escape hatch. Every one of the twenty-one cells is now a hard requirement, and a cell that cannot be executed leaves the release NO-GO rather than becoming preview.
scope.certified: All seven clients (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Windsurf, Gemini) on all three native platforms (darwin, linux, win32), each with a vendor runtime receipt for the exact candidate package.
scope.preview: Nothing. There is no preview tier for clients or platforms under version 3. Cross-device sync remains the only preview-scoped feature, and it is a feature, not a client cell.
scope.wsl: WSL is NOT a native Linux or Windows runtime. A receipt whose platform.wsl is true reports process.platform 'linux' from a Windows host and can never satisfy a native linux or win32 cell.
scope.clientVersions: clientVersionRequirements records the MINIMUM supported version of each client on each platform. The floors are operator-declared at freeze time: a floor is a support decision, not a measurement, and it is confirmed on first certification of that cell. Grounded anchors observed on the freezing host: Claude Code 2.1.269, codex-cli 0.148.0, cursor-agent 2026.08.25 (date-versioned), VS Code 3.19.19.
scope.crossDeviceSync: preview only; production promotion requires a separate decision and scope authorization.
scope.publication: A GO from this policy approves THE CANDIDATE against the full promise. Publishing additionally requires the tag workflow's aggregate over every osNodeCell below, over the twenty-one client cells, and over the deep-fuzz global receipt, all of which run on real runners and real vendor hosts.

fuzz.note: The deep sweep, not the smoke gate. A receipt naming fewer iterations than requiredIterations, or fewer extractors than minimumExtractors, is a smoke run wearing the deep receipt's name — the decision refuses it by that name rather than accepting the artifact's own summary.

freshness.failureTreatment: a missed transition or a timeout counts as a failed sample, never as a discarded one
freshness.configuration: production defaults — no shortened fallback, no overridden debounce
freshness.clock: from the source mutation to the moment every reader agrees — not to a capture or bookkeeping event
